skills.name: Military coups: change of ruler and constitutional legitimacy

note.text: A military coup is an unconstitutional seizure of state power involving armed forces. It differs from a change through the established electoral and constitutional process. Plotters may claim to end corruption or disorder, but a justification does not establish that the claim is true or that military government will deliver the promised remedy. Ghana’s overthrow of Nkrumah in 1966 is one historical example. Different coups had different actors, settings and consequences; military rule is not a synonym for every change of government.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish an unconstitutional military seizure from an elected transition and assess a justification critically. Builds on: institutional conflict and interacting causes of instability. Leads to: later evaluation of political and economic change.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: Original practice statement, not a historical quotation: An army council announces that it has taken control outside the normal constitutional rules and promises to restore order. The wording supports identifying a coup and a stated justification. It does not prove popular unanimity or a successful future outcome. A return to civilian officeholders also requires examination of institutions before it is called a democratic transition.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Every election that replaces a government is a military coup. Correction: An electoral transition follows a different mechanism.
A promise proves that the stated problem is solved already. Correction: The statement records an intention, not an achieved result.
Military rank automatically replaces every constitutional requirement. Correction: Rank and constitutional legitimacy are different matters.
A new ruler guarantees democratic participation for everyone. Correction: Institutions and actions need separate evidence.
